content.body:
Originally designed as an escort tank for recon platoons, the Somua S-35 was quickly recognized to be better than expected and in 1935 was adopted as the standard medium tank for the French army. In May 1940, it was regarded as the best medium tank in the world. Massing 13 tons with 40 mm of armor, a 47 mm cannon and a machine gun, it had a range of some 200 km and a top speed of 40 km/h. Its construction was novel, being made in four large castings and assembled quickly. It was well armed, well armored and speedy; it should have done better in combat than reports might suggest. On the battlefield it became sadly evident that all of these advantages were largely cancelled by the one-man turret and bad radio equipment: factors with little impact in a game environment like Battleground Europe, where the S-35 does very well, as it was expected it would from it's actual equipment specification.
The Somua is a fine tank, with good speed, smooth sighting while on the move, pretty good armor and a decent gun. It is able to deal directly with German medium tanks and win. As an S-35, you have the speed to flank the enemy, and the armor not to worry much about what he is doing while you flank him. Particularly vulnerable to rear-engine shots, you need to remember to check your 6 and keep your wits about you when in close range combat. Just don't give anyone that shot, and the S-35 will live up to its promises.
Make sure you don't accidentally open the gunner's port. On other tanks, this would leave a very small vulnerability in the mantlet; on French tanks it opens a gaping port on the entire back of the turret leaving your turret members entirely exposed to even pistol fire.
Control Variations: Driver zooms in on view slit with (numpad 0 or Ins key). No periscope, closing view slit armor blocks view completely. Commander is in a cupola, cannot unbutton. View is through an armored viewslit (key O to open). No view elevation change. View traverse speed limited to turret traverse speed.
